author: HBK
text_post: Hi mate no problem, I'm going to try and answer your question best I can, and if you have any questions on my answer please go ahead, I can't guarantee if I have the answer that will work for you but I can try, and I guess everyone on this board has a similar way of thinking. Ok, you ask firstly What if you have problems just making small talk with people?. I just want to be certain here that you absolutely know and understand that you do not need to join a martial arts club or any club at all that involves anything physical. The type of place you need to join should exist as long as you have means of travel and you don't live somewhere very remote or something. This is the criteria that the place you join has to meet:- - The club should have a mixture of people, male and female, doesn't necessarily matter if more guys than girls, but there should definitely be a mix. - It needs to be something that there are many occasions where you can talk. For example an an extreme sport lets say white water rafting for example, there would not be much opportunity because you'd just be on a raft screaming and etc, and then when you get changed later on people would be in segregated changing rooms, basically there would be not much opportunity for you to talk to anyone so I personally would not recommend something like that (I'm not saying no-one has ever met their partner doing this, but I'm gearing this towards us people) - The people need to be friendly and bubbly (males as well as the females) and the type of place you go MAY determine that. I've done martial arts, gymnastics and free running etc and they are fun things to do and make people happy. If you were to become an art critique and go to art show case etc I could possibly imagine people being a little bit more uptight and not relaxed (no offense to anyone, I may be totally wrong). - And absolutely MOST importantly of all, the main criteria the place needs to be meet, it needs to be something that you thoroughly enjoy and I mean really love, and either you are very good at it, or you have the potential to become very skilled at it (because of how much you enjoy it and become skilled through it, ideally something that you could "learn" or "teach"). This is the most essential thing and leads me on to your question about making small talk with people. As for places to join, only you can know what's best for you. To my friend in work who has slight problems and isn't very active, the only thing I could recommend for him was something like a cookery class. What if you have problems just making small talk with people? This is why I said that the most essential thing is being at some place that you enjoy what you're doing and you are very interested in learning. I'll just use cookery as the example for now because I don't know what else, I can't assume everyone is into martial arts and gymnastics like me. Ok, first of all, hopefully there would be some guys in the cookery class. You need to get to know them and have little pockets of convo with them, even if you ask them questions about how to perform a certain aspect of what you're doing on that day, "how much of that mixture do I put in here mate"? (mate, whatever the term is in your country, I'm in the UK). I don't know exactly how far back your confidence is, if you have problem making small talk with EVERYONE or just women? But if with everyone you have to overcome this somehow. Look at which guys look friendly and would be willing to answer a question, don't ask someone that looks miserable and moody and someone who is only interested in themselves or their own "bubble" group of friends. After you first visit, judge the type of people there, read some quick one or 2 lined jokes off the internet, some witty stuff which you could pop in a joke and make someone laugh, you'll definitely be in their good books (I'm talking about men still so don't worry). If you do make a male group of friends there, you've established that you can talk and have a chat and have a laugh with guys. Learn your craft (cookery in this case), be interested in it, learn about it when you're not in the class (like I said, you need genuine interest in what you're doing, you cannot be bored by it).  (Firstly you may find that whatever it is you get into, you'll think about it so much that you'll forget about the hurt of not being a with a girl, just ignore it and concentrate on becoming more skilled. Secondly, girls do like it when guys are so into something that they are completely focused on it and cannot be distracted by anything to take them away from what they're doing.) Anyway moving on, you need to do this until you're confidence in that place has built up. You are perfectly comfortable with where you are and what you're doing, you don't feel like a stranger, you know where everything is and you know what you're doing. Here is where you need to make the transition. For this part I am going to copy and paste a chunk of text from my original long post because it is so relevant and I don't think it needs altering:- Ok, what I would say, when you are in these type of places, start talking and chatting to girls that you DON'T fancy, just to get used to how they react and things to your sense of humour and the way you behave etc, if they give negative signals, don't behave that "way" again, if they act positively, you know what you've done is considered as "good" by a girl. Bear in mind, this is with girls that you DON'T fancy, you should have the balls to do this because its just like chatting to a guy, who gives a shit if they don't like you after it. When you can do this, try make friends with one/some of them, and try to make physical contact of SOME sort. For example, if they say they've been having a bad day, just pat them on the shoulder and tell them "it'll be ok" or some bollocks like that, at least you're getting into a stage where you can touch a girl without shitting yourself. This I would say was what was happening to me, but without me even realising it. You need this primary skill in order to EVER get anywhere with a girl you do like. That my friend, is the key thing and I HOPE can help you in answer to your question. Obviously there is more to this guide which is in my long post about what to do when you locate a girl that you DO find attractive, but you absolutely have to get to the above stage. By now you should feel comfortable in where you are. Again, lets say cookery JUST as the example but you can apply this to anything. Bring extra ingredients with you, basically bring extra of anything that could possibly be used in the scenario that you're in. Be FAST with your ears. GUY or GIRL says and you overhear them "oh no, I forgot to bring onions", you need to be the first one hearing that and the first one to step forward with the spare item that they need. Unless someone is a completely wanker, no matter how attractive or unattractive they think you are, they are going to note you down as a decent person. "here you go, here's an onion for you, if you need any more I'm sure I've got a couple of extras in my bag". That type of thing. Or on the reverse side, lets say you're stationed next to a girl, on the same kitchen counter or whatever "excuse me, how do I actually do this, I can't seem to get how to mix this dough correctly, it's just not working out the way the tutor explained" Either she will just verbally tell you which is a bit of a let down, or she may actually step in and show you. Again, for now I need you to understand that all of the above so far is only aimed at girls that you do not find attractive, in the slightest way, even girls that you consider particular unattractive if need be, You need to gauge the way girls react to your persona, and take out the bits that you get negative reactions to (making sure that the negative reaction was justified, some women are just complete bitches, and it won't be your fault, don't get knocked back from it). I remember teaching some females at the martial arts class I was out (I can't remember if my girlfriend was in the group or not). I said, "ok now, I am going to show you a technique called sasae tsurikomi (pronounced sass-eye sooree comb-ee), now I know what you're all thinking, if you're knackered in the middle of a grading and I say this to you, you're going to be so drained of energy the first thing you'll ask is "does that come with chips"? (chips in the UK are what what you call fries in America if that's where you are). They all laughed because it was short and sharp. You need stuff like this in you arsenal and if you are quick enough to reel a joke off, it needs to be something that completely matches and goes with an event that has just happened or something that has just been said, people will love it.  Sorry I went off on a bit of a tangent there, but anyway, use the above, try to apply it as best as you can, if you think of a different method of approach but you haven't tried it yet, ask me and I will see what I think. No, I am not an expert in pulling girls, what I AM is someone who is a logical thinker, and someone that suffered from one of the most crippling cases of love shyness possible and I thought of a process to get out of it. Please private message me to let me know if you've replied, because I do not log on here frequently, however if you send me a private message I am notified by email which I get pushed through to my phone straight away. I hope this helps you mate and again, even if you have any questions about what I have detailed above, like a particular aspect of it, ask and I will try my best to give you the advice even if I don't know the answer. Before you try this stuff though, just ask yourself, do you REALLY want to be alone, a looser and suffering all this time. Or do you really want to make a difference in your life? If you really want to make a difference, then DO what I said, spend the money it costs to become part of a social group, SPEND the money to travel there, BE interested in what you're doing and you'll make new friends and won't have the lingering feeling of hurt so much when you are alone, you'll be reading about your interests and how to improve yourself, SPEND the time effort and money in the gym making yourself look more appealing and being more confident, SPEND money on the best bottle of cologne you can think off and put a tiny squirt on before you go anywhere, it makes a huge difference, and make sure it's not a cologne you've bought that you heard women like, it has to be something YOU like the smell of also so you feel confident in yourself when you've showered and have just put it on (although read a review of it, make sure it's not a smell that women find particular bad). Let me know how it goes mate!

Please mate, don't feel that you are nitpicking, ask or criticize absolutely anything, I would prefer that you do, because when I used to read these so called "confidence" articles they would just give you a guide to follow and a lot of that stuff just didn't apply to me because I was too shy and felt SICK if I was about to talk to a woman that I fancied. You're a good person and you need to be around good people. If her tips worked and helped I would just look at her with a big amazed eyes and say "wow that's awesome I can't believe that makes so much difference, how do you know how to do that?" I'm sorry I forgot to mention this in my original post, but this sort of thing comes into the later stages, the stages where you've already learned how to make small talk with girls etc. But remember, just look really confused even if you know exactly what you're doing, be aware of who's watching you and if you see a girl looking at you and you're about to make a mistake, just hold your hands up in the air (depends on what skill you're learning) and look at your hands confusingly as if you don't know how to do what you're doing (even though you do), it may spark something in them to come and help you.
